name: W1
notes: Reputation-based placement, not a hands-on test — revisit once actually worn. SpinFit's flagship hybrid-bore tip: the swiveling silicone core is widely reported to give a more consistent, fatigue-free seal than fixed tips, and the wider bore opens up air/soundstage without gutting bass the way some wide-bore tips do. Considered a safe upgrade across most IEMs rather than a tip that colors tuning hard in one direction.

name: Sedna Earfit Mythril
notes: Reputation-based placement, not a hands-on test — revisit once actually worn. The metal-reinforced-nozzle variant of Azla's Sedna Earfit line; the rigid core is reported to tighten bass and sharpen treble extension versus the stock silicone version, at the cost of a slightly firmer, less plush feel in the ear than Crystal 2.

name: Sedna Earfit Crystal 2
notes: Reputation-based placement, not a hands-on test — revisit once actually worn. Clear-silicone sibling to Mythril; softer and more comfortable for long sessions, with a gentler bass lift and smoother treble than the metal-core version. Generally regarded as the more universally comfortable all-rounder of the two Sedna tips.

name: S&S Eartips
notes: Reputation-based placement, not a hands-on test — revisit once actually worn. Dunu's stock-accessory tip bundled with several of their IEMs — decent, dependable seal and comfort, but no strong sonic identity of its own. Solid default rather than a deliberate upgrade pick.

name: EBT
notes: Reputation-based placement, not a hands-on test — revisit once actually worn. Less mainstream than the others on this list, so confidence here is lower — flag if this doesn't match your experience. General impression: isolation and comfort can be strong when the fit lands, but sonic character is closer to neutral/stock than the Azla or SpinFit tips, and quality can feel less consistent unit-to-unit.

name: CoreIR Brass
notes: Reputation-based placement, not a hands-on test — revisit once actually worn. Less mainstream than the others on this list, so confidence here is lower — flag if this doesn't match your experience. Brass-reinforced core in the same family as the metal-core Azla tips; adds some treble sparkle and bass texture, but the firmer, heavier build is reported to feel less comfortable over long sessions than silicone-only tips.

name: Magic Form Tips
notes: Reputation-based placement, not a hands-on test — revisit once actually worn. Foam-style form tip: excellent seal and isolation since the foam expands to the canal shape, but that same foam damps treble and air noticeably, giving a warmer, more muffled top end than any silicone tip on this list. Foam also compresses and wears out faster than silicone over repeated use.
